The witness C-1175 observed non-Serb inhabitants, Croats and Hungarians, being interrogated, mistreated, and beaten and also detained by the TO and the members of the police unit command by Stricevic. Volunteers also came from Prigrevica to Dalj to interrogate and beat detainees. The witness made these observations during his time in the TO and during his subsequent visits. Could the sketch, tab 4 of Exhibit 517 be put to the witness. And could it be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it not under seal?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Oh, yes, it is. We can put it actually on the ELMO, just not showing the -- the initials on it. The reason why it's under seal, because of the initials being put to this. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, could you point out to us with a pointer in which building you worked and where the TO headquarter was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: For the record, the witness is pointing at a building indicated as local community building TO headquarter. And could you also point out the building where Milorad Stricevic was residing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the building on the right side behind the community building indicated as offices and prison. Yes. And the -- you mentioned that people were kept -- Hungarians and Croats were kept and beaten in this facility. Can you point out where you saw that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is pointing at the right side building where "prison" is indicated. You also mentioned volunteers from Prigrevica. Where did you see them beat people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Here, also in the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: The witness is again indicating that same building indicated as "prison." Yes, thank you. That's enough for this building. And just one additional point: Where is Prigrevica situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Prigrevica is between Apatin and Sombor.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Does that mean it's in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: In Serbia, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And these volunteers from Prigrevica, what did they look like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: They wore beards. They had Sajkaca caps on, the fur caps.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Were they associated to any politician or any political party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did they cooperate with the Dalj TO or Stricevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: They only came to see Stricevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll continue now with the summary. Following the fall of Vukovar, a large number of inhabitants from Vukovar were brought to Dalj by busses and trucks escorted by JNA. The busses and trucks were first taken to the JNA headquarters in Dalj, which was in the IPK Ratarstvo near the Dalj Railway Station. The women were then taken to the Red Cross and transferred to the Dalj Cinema for overnight accommodation and then sent by busses to Serbia. A group of men from Vukovar was detained in the Dalj police station that was situated in the building Stara Zadruga. Others were detained in the TO building or the building where Stricevic was located. From among the detainees from Vukovar held at the TO headquarter, the witness was able to obtain the release of individuals known to him by obtaining permission from Pavle Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In paragraph -- witness, in paragraph 16, in relation to your efforts to get one of your friends released, you said that you were afraid that something bad could happen to them. What did you fear could happen to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: I was afraid that perhaps the people from Prigrevica could get hold of them or people like them.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 of your statement, you referred to the JNA headquarter in Ilok. Did the JNA and the TO cooperate? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: To some extent they cooperated, but I don't really know much about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Did you see them meet, that is, Mr. Milanovic or -- and the JNA staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: I saw Milovanovic going to the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll continue with the summary. Several days after the fall of Vukovar, TO Commander Milanovic came to the witness's home and told him that he needed help with the burial of dead bodies. Witness C-1175 together with Milanovic and a third person drove to the Lovas Farm and observed approximately ten to eleven dead bodies wearing civilian clothing scattered on a slope leading towards the Danube River. The witness provided a sketch of the location indicating the place where he found the bodies. Milanovic told the witness that the victims had been killed by TO members from Borovo Selo. A police officer, Mr. Obradovic from Vukovar, also arrived and instructed the witness and that other person what to do with the bodies. With the assistance of this third person, Witness C-1175 loaded the partially decomposed bodies onto the shovel of an excavator. The excavator took the bodies to another place within the farm compound. The witness recognised one of the dead as a glazier and amateur photographer he knew from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Witness, one additional question: Did the police officer Obradovic explain why the bodies had to be removed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Well, he said, first of all, that they needed to be buried and that foreign monitors were expected, so that these bodies shouldn't be found there when they came.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are the questions that the Prosecution has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. 1175, you were born in Dalj; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No. I was born in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But during the time you're testifying about, you were living in Dalj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And all the things you're testifying about relate to Dalj; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was there any JNA unit in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: A unit came to PP Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: It's an agricultural cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did that unit arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: I can't tell you the exact date, but after the fall of Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Was that unit present when these events that you're testifying about took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: They were there in the cooperative.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And those JNA members, did they have anything to do with any illegal activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Up there as civilians we didn't really have much access. They were mostly within that compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that unit engaging in any kind of activities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that unit arresting or mistreating anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Judging by what I heard at the beginning, you were for a time a member of the Territorial Defence, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For how long were you a member of the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: For about a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When did you join the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Around the 25th of August, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: 1991. I see. Were only Serbs in the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But who else was in the TO, apart from the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: There would be one or two Hungarians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Any other ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And as a Serb, you joined voluntarily. Nobody mobilised you, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No. I volunteered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you left on a voluntary basis too.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: No one kept you. No one forced you to stay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Which means that the TO of Dalj, all the members of that TO, were local volunteers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they all from Dalj or were there people from the area surrounding it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: From Dalj -- mostly from Dalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And apart from those that were from Dalj, where were the others from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: There were some from Erdut.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see, from the environs, in other words.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you say that problems between Serbs and Croats in Dalj started around March 1991; is that right, Mr. 1175?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please: Do you mean, when you use the word "problems", some sort of armed conflict or do you mean other problems?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Armed conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. So in March 1991.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And who provoked those armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: I think the Croats started it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: There was exchange of fire. There were quarrels and fights break out, and then people were taken into custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Taken into custody by the Croatian police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And up until the 1990 elections and the formation of the new police force, was it peaceful in Dalj and were relations among the population good?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And there were no inter-ethnic clashes, hatred, quarrels, and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From your statement, I see that some Croats in the village started receiving weapons; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As I understand it, these weapons were brought in in a TAM truck and then distributed among the Croats.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea as to the quantity of weapons that were distributed to the Croatian inhabitants of Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Well, quite a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you be a bit more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: A hundred or so barrels, for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "barrels," you mean automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And before they were armed, that is, before this incident occurred when you mentioned the TAM truck bringing in weapons, were there any incidents provoked by the Serbs against the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were there any incidents by the Croats against Serbs before this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, there were provocations and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, after the weapons were distributed, what started to happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how to call them. Their patrols and guards started roaming the streets and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that as early as April 1991 - because you said that the clashes started already in March - that in Dalj a number of Serbs were arrested and taken to Osijek? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that they were badly beaten up over there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any idea what could have prompted their arrest and beating in prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did they do something that -- at least that you knew about or heard about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, why, then, in your opinion, were they arrested and taken there and beaten up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: It is very difficult to explain the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the incident in April, when a certain number of Serbs were arrested and taken away and beaten up, did this cause serious concern among the Serb population of Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did people spontaneously rally in front of the police building in Dalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What happened then? The people gathered there and they came to protest, to inquire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, they demanded their immediate release.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But there was no violence then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No, there was no violence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, what was the response they were given?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: The response was that they would be released shortly and they did release them in the afternoon around 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And then you found out that they had been beaten up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What did they tell you? Did you speak to any one of them? What did they want from them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Allegedly they found them in the park. They took them into custody and beat them up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Because they were sitting in the park?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: From what I heard, they arrested them in the park.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Apart from this incident, do you recall - and this incident obviously contributed to the concern of the Serb population in Dalj, as you confirmed - do you recall the event that took place in Borovo Selo, a neighbouring village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did this incident, too, have a negative effect on the feeling and mood and did it prompt the fear among the Serbs in the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that a serious conflict, armed conflict occurred then between the Croatian police, which had attacked the Serb population of Borovo Selo? Was that what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please: Is it correct to say that they broke into the village and opened fire on the citizens?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Without any prior warning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Without any prior warning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And this happened in the very centre of Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, the very centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is the information I have correct, Mr. 1175, as this was in your neighbourhood, that they killed one of the locals and in the clinic they held hostage women and the staff of the outpatients clinic and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that through the intervention of a JNA unit these Croatian soldiers or, rather, policemen were saved and they were allowed to leave the village? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of your own knowledge, is the announcement correct issued by the command of the 1st Army the next day, that the members of the JNA during the tragic events in Borovo Selo did not use firearms nor did they fire a single shot but that thanks to the engagement of the JNA unit, armed conflicts were prevented and further bloodshed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this incident you are aware of that took place in your neighbourhood. The JNA arrived and without using weapons managed to stop the conflict and save the Croatian policemen that had attacked the citizens of Borovo Selo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the fact that after this fortunately unsuccessful operation in Borovo Selo groups were organised to terrorise the Serb population, groups for silent liquidations, as they were known?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about the victims of those groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that on the 3rd of May, 1991 the Sareka

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: from Borovo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1991, the Krajisk [phoen] coffee bar was blown up, also the property of a Serb; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And on the 6th of May, a coffee bar called Tufo [phoen], and there were various other planted mines and armed attacks on property owned by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were those acts which should have made it clear to the Serbs that they should leave, that they were unwanted there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS C-1175
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: And that appears to be an appropriate time to break off. Mr. Milosevic, you will have you have to three-quarters of an hour more cross-examination, if you require it, tomorrow. Witness C-1175, could you remember not to speak to anybody about your evidence during the adjournment, and don't speak to anybody until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Could you be back, please, at 9.00 tomorrow morning to conclude your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 28th day of August, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
